newsitem.title: FINLAND: ICE HOCKEY-RUSSIA BEAT SWEDEN TO HELP CZECH CAUSE.
newsitem.headline: ICE HOCKEY-RUSSIA BEAT SWEDEN TO HELP CZECH CAUSE.

text.p: Russia and the United States posted upset wins over the reigning Olympic and world champions on Monday opening up the race for medals at the ice hockey world championships.

Russia scored once in each of the first two periods then rode the goaltending of Maxim Mikhailovski to a 4-1 win over Sweden. It was the Olympic champions' first loss of the tournament having gone through round-robin play undefeated.
Earlier in the day, Ted Donato of the Boston Bruins scored a pair of second period goals as the United States held on to beat defending champions, the Czech Republic, 4-3.
Although it was only the first game of the medal round, it was a "must-win" for the U.S. who were the only one of six teams not to carry over any points from the round-robin.
Sweden, the only team to come through with the maximum four points, have now seen their advantage wiped out but they still cling to a share of first place with Russia.
Canada, the Czech Republic, United States and Finland trail with two.

The Russians who, as the Soviet Union, won 20 titles and eight Olympic gold medals, have failed to reach the podium in the last three championships. But they rekindled memories of the past as they turned in their best two-way effort of the tournament against the Swedes.
Alexei Morozov opened the scoring midway through the first period, splitting two Swedish defenders and rifling a wrist-shot in off goaltender Tommy Salo.
With just 57 seconds remaining in the second period, Alexei Yashin of the Ottawa Senators collect the winner when he charged down the slot and redirected Oleg Belov's pass by Salo.
Alexander Prokopyev and Alexander Barkov added third period insurance goals before Anders Carlson ruined Mikhailovski's shutout bid with a powerplay goal with less than two minutes to play.
"I didn't feel we had the game won until after the third goal," said Russian coach Igor Dmitriev.
In the day's opening match, the United States held off a determined comeback bid by the Czech Republic.
Leading 4-1 entering the final period, the Americans sat back and allowed the Czechs to strike two goals in the opening three minutes, Vladimir Vujtek and Jiri Dopita scoring 48 seconds apart.

Following the second goal, U.S. coach Jeff Jackson immediately called a time-out to calm his troops. It seemed to have the desired effect and the Americans were finally able to celebrate a crucial win.
"I was concerned," said Jackson. "We've had problems in the third period all tournament.
"I thought our team played well for 40 minutes and then fell asleep between the second and third."
Boston Bruins defenceman Bob Beers scored the only goal of the first period, stabbing Donald Barshear's pass past Roman Cechmanek to give the Americans the 1-0 lead.
In the second, Donato and Chris Marinucci put the U.S. 3-0 up before Vujtek finally got the Czechs on the scoreboard.
Donato, collected his second of the period, and what proved to be the winner, 56 seconds later when he blasted a slap shot between Cechmanek's pads to restore the Americans' three-goal advantage.
